teaser: One agent's eleven rules, moved from the prompt into hooks and tested: four fully, two mostly, three partly, two not at all, and a gap in the leak scan.
core_idea: Most agent rules are hope-based security kept by the model; tested rule by rule on this site's own behaviour policy, hooks could keep four of eleven rules fully and two mostly, which makes them the sweet spot until enforcement moves off the machine, because they are the first layer that does not rely on the model and the last that sees the action as the agent meant it, provided the organisation installs them where the agent cannot write and sets them to fail closed; existing packs block dangerous commands, and the missing step is generating tested hooks from a written policy so the same rows can later compile to a gateway such as one built on OWASP's Agent Control Standard.

quotes.text: A hook is only as good as the check it runs.
A hook pack should be a set of independent checks, not a pipeline.
quotes.why: What parallel hooks and deny-wins precedence imply.

quotes.text: every rule with no hook is still hope, and every hook with no rule is a control nobody can explain.
